mainTopic: How much of a dead person's bones and blood makes a נזיר shave: the רובע of bones from a spine and skull, the old dispute about רובע and רביעית, and what the משנה's words על אלו leave out.
overview: The גמרא is asking whether a רובע (quarter-קב) of bones from a spine and skull makes a נזיר impure so that he must shave. It first deals with an apparent contradiction in רבא's views and answers that he changed his mind after hearing רבי עקיבא. It then tries to prove the answer from שמאי, who says even one bone from the spine or skull is impure. Both possible proofs from שמאי are pushed away, so neither side is proven. Next, רבי אליעזר reports that the early זקנים argued about whether a רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood make impure in every way. A later בית דין ruled that these smaller amounts count for תרומה and קדשים, but not for a נזיר or for someone bringing the קרבן פסח. The גמרא asks how a middle opinion like this can decide a dispute, and answers that it was a tradition from חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. Finally, the גמרא explains what the words על אלו in the משנה leave out, and quotes the next item in the list, a חצי קב of bones.

steps.title: רבא seems to say the opposite elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the use of רבא's view by quoting another statement of רבא. That statement suggests a רובע of bones from a spine and skull does bring טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it רבא himself who said: this was needed only for a spine and skull that don't have a רובע of bones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא said something elsewhere that seems to contradict how his view was just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a certain teaching was needed only for a spine and skull that have less than a רובע of bones. That suggests that with a full רובע, everyone agrees there is טומאה. So רבא seems to hold that a רובע from a spine and skull is impure, which clashes with the earlier picture of his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Spine, backbone
Skull
A quarter-קב of bones, a measure of bones that brings טומאה
It was needed only for… (a teaching applies to a specific case)

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rava himself who said:
for a spine and a skull
that do not contain a quarter-kav of bones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier use of רבא's view, which comes just before this part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier understanding of רבא's position
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's other statement implies a רובע from spine and skull is impure, so he seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: רבא changed his mind after hearing רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא made his first statement before hearing רבי עקיבא's teaching. After hearing it, he changed his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was before; after he heard it from רבי עקיבא, he changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying רבא's two statements come from different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction because רבא retracted. Once he heard how רבי עקיבא's case was really set up, he understood things differently and gave up his first statement.

keyTerms.meaning: After he heard it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the two statements come from different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds two opposite views at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's later view, after hearing רבי עקיבא, replaces his earlier statement.
steps.whatToRemember: When a אמורא seems to contradict himself, one answer is that he changed his mind (בתר דשמעה).

steps.title: Trying to prove it from שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמאי's view that even one bone from the spine or skull brings טומאה. It hopes this shows the רבנן would at least agree about a רובע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמאי says one bone from the spine or from the skull brings טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמאי says even a single bone is enough, the רבנן who argue with him probably don't hold something wildly different. So the hope is that they at least agree a רובע of bones brings טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a source as proof
One single bone

phrases.notes: He means even this one bone brings טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attempt to settle the question of a רובע from a spine and skull.
steps.raayaObject: That a רובע of bones from a spine and skull brings טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמאי's ruling that even one bone from the spine or skull is impure

steps.title: שמאי is extra strict, so no proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. שמאי is especially strict, so we cannot learn the רבנן's view from his.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי is different, because he is very strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי's ruling comes from his own extra strictness. So it tells us nothing about where the רבנן stand. They might be far more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Very strict, more strict than others

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמאי's view comes from his special strictness, so it cannot show what the רבנן hold.

steps.title: Then prove the opposite: the רבנן need a חצי קב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the rejection around. If שמאי is unusually strict, maybe the רבנן are very lenient and require a full חצי קב of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us resolve it from here: it is only שמאי who is strict, so the רבנן would need a half-קב of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the last answer to try to prove the opposite side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמאי's view is only because he is extra strict, then the רבנן must be lenient. Then a רובע would not be enough, and only a חצי קב from the spine and skull would bring טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us resolve (the question) from it
But according to the רבנן, an inference from the opposite
Half a קב, double a רובע

phrases.english: the reason is Shammai's, since he is stringent;
not until there is a half-kav of bones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rejection in step 4 to argue the opposite result.
steps.raayaObject: That a רובע from a spine and skull does NOT bring טומאה for the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the claim that only שמאי is strict
steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the conclusion. The גמרא is only testing the opposite side, and it gets pushed away right after.

steps.title: Maybe the רבנן only argue about one bone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this too. Maybe the רבנן argue with שמאי only about a single bone, but agree that a רובע of bones brings טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the רבנן argue with שמאי only about one bone, but about a רובע of bones even the רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof as well, so the question is still open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight between שמאי and the רבנן might be narrow: only whether one bone is enough. That leaves room for the רבנן to agree that a רובע is impure. So neither side can be proven from שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, which introduces another possibility
They only disagree up to here, which limits how far an argument goes
They agree

phrases.english: but regarding a quarter-kav of bones —

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּשַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that the רבנן require a half-קב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument may be limited to a single bone, so it says nothing about a רובע.
steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof from שמאי works. The רבנן might be lenient, or they might agree that a רובע is enough, so the question of a רובע from a spine and skull stays open.

steps.title: The early Elders argued about a quarter of bones and blood
steps.stepSummary: ר' אליעזר reports that the early זקנים were split. Some said only a חצי קב of bones and a חצי לוג of blood make impure in every way. Others said even a רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: Some of the early זקנים used to say that a חצי קב of bones and a חצי לוג of blood make impure in every way, but a רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood do not. Others among them said that even a רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood make impure in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from ר' אליעזר describing an old argument among the early זקנים about the smaller amounts of bones and blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the bigger amounts (חצי קב of bones, חצי לוג of blood) make impure in every way. The argument is only about the smaller amounts (רובע and רביעית). This connects to the earlier question of what the רבנן hold about a רובע of bones.

keyTerms.meaning: The early Elders, sages of earlier generations
A quarter (here, a quarter of a קב of bones)
A quarter (here, a quarter of a לוג of blood)
For everything, meaning it makes impure in every way
Half a לוג, a liquid measure

phrases.english: some of them used to say:

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי קַב עֲצָמוֹת וַחֲצִי לוֹג דָּם
phrases.english: half a kav of bones and half a log of blood

phrases.notes: He means they make a person impure in every way, even just by being under the same roof as them.

phrases.english: a quarter of bones and a quarter of blood
And some of them used to say:
even a quarter of bones and a quarter of blood

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing what the רבנן hold about a רובע of bones, the גמרא brings an old dispute about exactly that amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The early זקנים argued about whether a רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood make impure in every way.

steps.title: The later court ruled in between
steps.stepSummary: The בית דין that came after the זקנים ruled that the smaller amounts make impure for תרומה and קדשים, but not for a נזיר or for someone bringing the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית דין after them said: a חצי קב of bones and a חצי לוג of blood make impure in every way. A רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood make impure for תרומה and קדשים, but not for a נזיר or for someone bringing the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues: a later בית דין gives a middle ruling between the two older opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the bigger amounts, nothing changes. For the smaller amounts, the later court split the law. They count for תרומה and קדשים, but a נזיר does not have to shave because of them, and they do not stop someone from bringing the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The court that came after them
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Holy offerings
Someone bringing the קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The later court's rule: a רובע of bones or a רביעית of blood makes impure for תרומה and קדשים, but not for a נזיר or for the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: The court that came after them said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי קַב עֲצָמוֹת וַחֲצִי לוֹג דָּם
phrases.english: half a kav of bones and half a log of blood
a quarter of bones and a quarter of blood
But not for a nazir or for one who brings the Pesach offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same teaching with the later court's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רובע of bones and a רביעית of blood make impure for תרומה and קדשים, but not for a נזיר or the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: A middle opinion cannot decide a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the later court: there is a rule that a third, in-between opinion does not count as deciding between two others.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a third opinion that splits the difference is not considered a decision!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the later court's ruling, because a compromise opinion normally cannot settle an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later court took a middle path that neither side said: yes for תרומה and קדשים, no for נזיר and פסח. Normally such a new third view does not count as deciding the dispute. So how could this ruling become the הלכה?

keyTerms.meaning: But now consider (opens a challenge)
A third, in-between opinion
Decides, settles the dispute

phrases.english: But now, a decision of a third opinion is not a decision!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the later court's middle ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The later בית דין's split ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A compromise third opinion cannot decide between two earlier opinions.

steps.title: The ruling was a tradition from the prophets
steps.stepSummary: ר' יעקב בר אידי answers that the later court did not invent a compromise. They said it from a tradition going back to חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said: They said it from a received tradition, from חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the later ruling was a tradition handed down, not a new compromise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against a third opinion applies to a new middle view made up to settle a dispute. Here, the ruling came from a tradition going back to the last prophets. So it stands on its own and is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: From a received tradition
The last three prophets

steps.whatToRemember: The later court's split ruling is valid because it was a tradition from חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, not a made-up compromise.

phrases.english: They said it from a received tradition:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי, מִפִּי שְׁמוּעָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the later court.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the source of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later court made up a compromise, which should not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling was a tradition from the prophets, so it is valid.

steps.title: The first על אלו leaves out the barley-grain bone under a roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words על אלו הנזיר מגלח. It explains that על אלו in the first part leaves out a barley-grain-sized bone when the נזיר is only under the same roof as it. A נזיר shaves for touching or carrying it, but not for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For these a נזיר shaves.' The words 'for these' in the first part come to leave out a bone the size of a barley grain. For touching it and carrying it, yes; for being under the same roof as it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now returns to the משנה and explains what the words על אלו in the first part come to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for these' mean only the cases listed, and not others. A barley-grain-sized bone makes a נזיר shave if he touches or carries it. It does not make him shave if he is only under the same roof as it (אהל).

keyTerms.meaning: For these (only these)
The first part of the משנה
A bone the size of a barley grain
Touching and carrying
Being under the same roof or covering as the impure item

phrases.english: The words 'for these' of the first part
come to leave out a bone the size of a barley grain,
for touching it and carrying it, yes,
but for being under a roof with it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר does not shave for being under a roof with a barley-grain-sized bone, only for touching or carrying it.

steps.title: The second על אלו leaves out the covering stone
steps.stepSummary: The words על אלו in the last part of the משנה leave out an אבן הסכוכית, a covering stone. A נזיר does not shave because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the words 'for these' of the last part come to leave out a covering stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the second על אלו, in the last part of the משנה, comes to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each על אלו in the משנה teaches its own exception. The second one teaches that a covering stone does not make a נזיר shave.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
A covering stone

steps.whatToRemember: Each על אלו excludes something: the first leaves out a barley-grain-sized bone under the same roof, and the second leaves out a covering stone.

phrases.english: And the words 'for these' of the last part —
come to leave out a covering stone.
phrases.notes: This is a stone that forms a cover over a dead body.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל אֵלּוּ דְּסֵיפָא לְמַעוֹטֵי אֶבֶן הַסָּכוֹכִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second על אלו, matching the explanation of the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר does not shave because of an אבן הסכוכית.

steps.title: Quoting the next item in the list: a חצי קב of bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and a half-קב of bones' to begin a new discussion about this item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and a half-קב of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a short phrase from the משנה's list of things a נזיר shaves for. This line sets up the next discussion; nothing is explained yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא talked about the words על אלו at the start and end of the משנה. Now it picks up one specific item from the list, half a קב of bones. It quotes this item so it can analyze it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a קב, a measure of volume. Here it is the amount of a dead person's bones that brings טומאה.
Bones, here meaning the bones of a dead person.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. The גמרא is only quoting the משנה to get ready for its next point.

phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה's list of things that make a נזיר shave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing what the words על אלו leave out, the גמרא turns to a specific item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists a half-קב of bones as one of the things a נזיר shaves for. The גמרא quotes it to discuss it next.
